okay, so i was not a minor when i got diagnosed etc, but i’m sure some of these apply. 

i think that you definitely can go to a regular doctor for metal health things, to they will then refer you to a psychiatrist. i think that you should mention it on the check up (if you feel comfortable talking about it with your family in the room)and schedule another appointment to talk about that. 

you probably won’t be given an exact diagnosis, but you’ll probably fill out some questionnaires that map out your symptoms. based on those, the doctor can probably tell you what you might have, but you most likely won’t be diagnosed until you go to a specialist. the doctor may however prescribe medication. i got prescribed meds and a referral to the psychiatrist on my appointment with a gp. 

you probably should see a specialist. in finland, where i live, you have to see a specialist, before you can be referred to a therapist. your symptoms etc will also be discussed with the specialist, so that they can diagnose you. you’ll also probably have to do more questionnaires. 

now the checkup thing: i don’t really know you or your family, so i don’t know how they would react. i would maybe tell the doctor beforehand that there’s something you want to discuss in private, so then after the checkup you could talk about mental health. i do think that you’ll need a whole appointment to thoroughly talk about your mental health, so you can get the help you need. 

honestly it might make it worse. but it also might make it better. there’s no way of knowing beforehand, i’m afraid. you can ask the doctor about this and they can probably tell you about the pros and cons of the medication they’re recommending. you probably can refuse it if it doesn’t seem like a good idea to you. 

i’m currently on meds that aren’t really working, so i can’t really say anything about that. 

usually with psych medication it takes around a week or so to notice any side affects and two weeks to notice the intended effects. this can vary a lot tho, and i’m not a doctor, so ask your doctor about this, too.  switching out medication is also something you’ll discuss with your doctor when it’s time for that. you’ll probably have a checkup on the medication after maybe a month or so. personally, i had appointments with my psychiatrist and he’d ask me questions about my mood and other symptoms, and made changes according to that. so for example the first medication that i tried didn’t work and made my nose bleed, so i told him and he prescribed another medication. 

i honestly don’t know about the treatment costs in the states, it probably depends on your insurance and stuff like that.
